title: Fix the Mismatched String Specifier
description: The program should print an integer count using printf.
actualProblem: %s tells printf to treat the argument as a pointer to a null-terminated string, but count is a plain int, not an address. printf tries to read a string starting at whatever memory address the integer 42 happens to represent, which is undefined behavior (often a crash).
explanation: Each printf format specifier expects a specific argument type: %d for int, %s for a char* string, %f for float/double, and so on. Using the wrong specifier misinterprets the bytes of the argument, with unpredictable results.
